raw_generated_sections.policy_title: Information Security Policy for M004 policy-eval corpus - Four-person fully remote company

sections.content: This policy establishes baseline information security practices for M004 policy-eval corpus - Four-person fully remote company. It applies to all staff, contractors, and third parties who handle company information or use company resources. The policy governs how information is accessed, protected, stored, and shared across remote work environments.

The Founder, Priya Shah, is responsible for overall information security governance. The security responsible role is assigned to Priya Shah, who ensures compliance with security controls and oversight of policy execution. Senior leadership, including Priya Shah, is accountable for supporting security initiatives and ensuring resource availability for security operations.

All user accounts must use multi-factor authentication (MFA) for access to company systems and services. MFA is mandatory for all staff accounts and privileged accounts. Access to sensitive systems must be granted only on a need-to-know basis, with no separation of privileged access currently implemented. Staff must never share credentials or allow others to use their accounts.

All devices used for company work must be protected with endpoint protection software. Devices must be updated with security patches promptly; patching is expected to occur when staff restart their devices, but is not enforced automatically. Device encryption is not currently implemented and is not confirmed. All staff must ensure devices are locked or secured when not in use, especially during remote work.

All important business information must be backed up appropriately. Backups are currently performed, but the method and frequency are not formally documented. Confidential and personal information must be handled with care, stored securely, and only shared when necessary and authorized. Information must not be stored on personal devices unless explicitly approved and encrypted.

The organisation operates fully remotely. All staff work from home or other remote locations. Remote access to company systems is controlled and monitored. Staff must ensure their work environment is secure, including using secure internet connections and avoiding public workspaces when handling sensitive information. All work-related activities must occur within the approved remote work framework.

Any suspected security incident, including phishing attempts, unauthorized access, or data loss, must be reported immediately to the security responsible (Priya Shah). The incident reporting route is in place and staff are expected to use it. No incident may be ignored or downplayed. All reports must be documented and escalated for review.

This policy is reviewed annually or upon significant changes to operations, security state, or governance. It is approved by the policy authoriser, Priya Shah, and is subject to version control. The current version is documented and accessible to all staff. Any updates to the policy must be communicated formally to all relevant personnel.

Devices used for remote work must be encrypted and compliant with organisational security standards. Staff working from home must ensure physical workspaces are secure and not accessible to unauthorised persons.

Any suspected or actual security incident must be reported immediately to the organisation’s designated incident reporting route. Staff must not delay reporting due to uncertainty. The incident reporting route is confirmed to exist, and all staff must be trained to identify and report potential incidents.

This policy is approved by the Chief Operating Officer, Freya Lindqvist. Physical access to office areas must be restricted to authorised personnel only. Remote workers must use secure, monitored networks and avoid public Wi-Fi for sensitive tasks.
